relationships.description: Belimumab directly binds and neutralizes soluble BAFF (BLyS), preventing B cell survival signaling
Anifrolumab blocks the type I interferon receptor IFNAR1, suppressing the IFN gene signature
Voclosporin inhibits calcineurin, blocking NFAT-mediated T cell activation
Tacrolimus binds FKBP12 and inhibits calcineurin, blocking T cell activation
Hydroxychloroquine inhibits endosomal TLR7 activation by preventing endosome acidification
Hydroxychloroquine inhibits endosomal TLR9 activation by preventing endosome acidification
Rituximab depletes CD20+ B cells through ADCC, CDC, and apoptosis
Obinutuzumab is a type II anti-CD20 antibody with enhanced direct cell death and reduced CDC vs rituximab
Mycophenolate mofetil inhibits IMPDH, blocking de novo purine synthesis in lymphocytes
Baricitinib inhibits JAK1, blocking type I IFN, IL-6, and other cytokine signaling
Prednisone binds glucocorticoid receptor (NR3C1), broadly suppressing NF-κB and inflammatory gene transcription
BAFF is a critical survival factor in B cell receptor signaling and B cell homeostasis
BLK is a Src-family kinase essential for B cell receptor signal transduction
BANK1 is a scaffold protein that modulates BCR-induced calcium mobilization
BTK is an essential kinase for BCR and Fc receptor signaling in B cells and myeloid cells
IRF5 is a master transcription factor driving type I IFN production downstream of TLR7/TLR9
IFNAR1 is the receptor subunit for type I interferons, mediating all IFN-α/β signaling
TLR7 senses ssRNA in endosomes and triggers IRF5/IRF7-mediated IFN-α production
TLR9 senses CpG DNA in endosomes and triggers IRF5/IRF7-mediated IFN-α production
JAK1 mediates signaling for type I IFNs, IL-6, and other γ-chain cytokines
TYK2 mediates type I IFN and IL-12/IL-23 signaling through JAK-STAT pathways
STAT4 mediates IL-12 and type I IFN-induced transcription, promoting Th1/Th17 differentiation
TNFAIP3 (A20) negatively regulates NF-κB signaling through ubiquitin editing; loss of function drives inflammation
ITGAM encodes CD11b, a component of complement receptor 3 (CR3) critical for immune complex clearance
FCGR2A mediates IgG immune complex binding and clearance by phagocytes
FCGR3A mediates ADCC and immune complex clearance
TNFSF4 (OX40L) provides costimulatory signals that enhance T cell activation and Tfh function
PTPN22 (LYP) negatively regulates T cell receptor signaling; R620W variant alters T cell selection thresholds
TLR7 is a key endosomal sensor of ssRNA that drives the lupus IFN signature
TLR9 is a key endosomal sensor of CpG DNA that drives B cell activation in lupus
IRF5 is activated downstream of TLR7/TLR9-MyD88 signaling to drive IFN-α production
Belimumab modulates B cell signaling by reducing BAFF-dependent B cell survival
Anifrolumab blocks type I interferon signaling by binding IFNAR1
Hydroxychloroquine inhibits endosomal TLR7 and TLR9 activation
Baricitinib inhibits JAK1/JAK2, broadly suppressing cytokine-driven JAK-STAT signaling
The type I interferon pathway is a central driver of SLE pathogenesis, with ~60-80% of patients showing an IFN gene signature
Dysregulated B cell signaling drives autoantibody production and immune complex formation in SLE
Aberrant JAK-STAT signaling downstream of multiple cytokines contributes to lupus inflammation
Endosomal TLR sensing of self-nucleic acids is a key initiating event in the lupus autoimmune response
Chronic NF-κB activation drives sustained inflammation and tissue damage in SLE
Defective complement-mediated clearance of apoptotic debris leads to autoantigen exposure and immune activation
Enhanced T cell costimulation drives Tfh expansion and autoreactive B cell help in SLE
HLA-DRB1 is the strongest genetic risk factor for SLE, with specific alleles conferring 2-3x increased risk
IRF5 risk haplotypes are associated with high serum IFN-α activity and increased SLE susceptibility
STAT4 rs7574865 risk variant is associated with increased SLE susceptibility and severity
ITGAM missense variants impair phagocytosis and are associated with increased SLE risk
TNFAIP3 loss-of-function variants reduce NF-κB regulation and increase SLE risk
Belimumab is FDA-approved for SLE and lupus nephritis; reduces disease activity and flare risk
Anifrolumab is FDA-approved for moderate to severe SLE; reduces disease activity and corticosteroid use
Hydroxychloroquine is the standard-of-care for all SLE patients; reduces flares and improves survival
Voclosporin is FDA-approved for lupus nephritis in combination with MMF and corticosteroids
Rituximab is used off-label for refractory SLE; depletes CD20+ B cells
Tacrolimus is used off-label for lupus nephritis, especially in Asian populations
Azathioprine is a steroid-sparing maintenance therapy for lupus nephritis and SLE
Cyclophosphamide is reserved for severe organ-threatening lupus including nephritis, CNS, and pulmonary involvement
Mycophenolate is a first-line induction and maintenance therapy for lupus nephritis
Acalabrutinib is a highly selective BTK inhibitor that suppresses BCR signaling, reducing B cell activation and autoantibody production
Avacopan blocks C5aR, intercepting C5a-mediated neutrophil recruitment and inflammation downstream of complement activation
Cyclosporine binds cyclophilin and inhibits calcineurin, blocking NFAT-mediated T cell activation
Dimethyl fumarate activates Nrf2 and inhibits NF-κB nuclear translocation, reducing proinflammatory gene expression
Iscalimab blocks CD40-CD40L costimulation, preventing T cell-dependent B cell help and germinal center formation
Ravulizumab binds C5 and blocks terminal complement activation, preventing C5a and MAC-mediated tissue damage
Rozanolixizumab blocks FcRn, reducing pathogenic IgG levels and decreasing immune complex substrate for complement activation
Tofacitinib inhibits JAK1, broadly blocking type I IFN, IL-6, IL-12/IL-23, and other cytokine signaling
Tofacitinib broadly suppresses JAK-STAT signaling downstream of multiple proinflammatory cytokine receptors
